answer: A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, and therefore paying the walnut bond on all of them and exposing each to the jetty slash. Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 10 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. Because the reef audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. Slashing removes 98 percent at once. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
